_meta.description: The ratio registry (docs/m4-spec.md section 2.1). Each ratio names its formula and inputs so a reader can repeat the arithmetic. Values are computed by the engine each time, never stored.

ratios.name: Savings rate
ratios.formula: saving divided by take-home pay, in the first full year
ratios.sentence: You save {value} of your take-home pay.

bands.words: most of your pay is spoken for

ratios.name: The gap
ratios.formula: take-home minus spending minus debt payments, a year
ratios.sentence: After spending and debt payments, {value} a year is left to save.

ratios.name: Years of spending saved
ratios.formula: net worth divided by a year of spending
ratios.sentence: Your net worth covers {value} of spending.

ratios.name: FI progress
ratios.formula: total assets divided by the FI number (assets at the FI date)
ratios.sentence: You are {value} of the way to your FI number.

ratios.name: Effective tax rate
ratios.formula: all taxes divided by gross income, in the first full year
ratios.sentence: Taxes take {value} of your gross income this year.

ratios.name: Real hourly wage
ratios.formula: take-home pay divided by hours worked (2,000 a year when hours are not entered)
ratios.sentence: After taxes, an hour of your work is worth about {value}.

ratios.name: Runway
ratios.formula: the Level 2 runway stack at full spending
ratios.sentence: With no income, your runway is about {value}.

ratios.name: Debt-to-income
ratios.formula: yearly debt payments divided by gross income
ratios.sentence: Debt payments take {value} of your gross income.

ratios.name: Housing share
ratios.formula: housing and utilities divided by take-home pay
ratios.sentence: Housing takes {value} of your take-home pay.

ratios.name: Dream load
ratios.formula: the years every dream adds to the FI date, in all
ratios.sentence: Your dreams together move your FI date by {value}.

ratios.name: Tax efficiency ratio
ratios.formula: lifetime taxes divided by lifetime gross income and withdrawals, over the whole plan
ratios.sentence: Over your whole plan, taxes take {value} of every dollar that comes in.

ratios.name: True FI gap
ratios.formula: Gross FI (25 times spending) minus Net FI (assets at the optimized FI date)
ratios.sentence: Doing the homework is worth {value} of FI number.

ratios.name: Heirs' share
ratios.formula: estate after heirs' taxes divided by the estate before them
ratios.sentence: Of what you leave, heirs keep about {value} after their taxes.

lenses.name: The 4% rule
lenses.idea: 25 times spending is the number everyone optimizes toward. Money Rooms finds what the number actually is.

lenses.name: Shockingly simple math
lenses.idea: Your savings rate alone sets your years to FI, at one assumed return.
lenses.source: Mr. Money Mustache, The Shockingly Simple Math Behind Early Retirement (2012); the table is recomputed from its stated 5% real return and 4% withdrawal rate

lenses.name: The DRAFTT scorecard
lenses.idea: Six letters of the budget as shares of take-home: Debt, Rent, Automobile, Food, Therapy, Taxes.

lenses.name: Hours
lenses.idea: Every cost in hours of your real hourly wage.

lenses.name: Taxes
lenses.idea: What the IRS takes over a lifetime, and the strategies that change it.
